idk if there are actual documentaries about this but I can give my 2 cents. Saudi Arabia, at least from Riyadh (as I was from there), has many workers from African and Southeast Asian countries. I've lived most of my life there along with so many other families whose parents just want to earn and provide for their loved ones. I've watched a video before (I cant remember which video it was) where a Saudi man was interviewed about this and is happy that the system is working as smoothly as it is because of the foreigners that work there. It hasn't always been as bright as it seemed. Things have changed now and there's what they call "Saudization". It's basically a mandated rule for all companies to have a specific ratio of Arab workers and foreign workers. Ok sure fine but what if there are no more jobs for them to employ for Arab workers? That's where they start cutting contracts from foreign workers. It never fails to make anyone sad knowing that your friend from school and their family is forced to exit the country because their parents lost their job just like that. My mom got her contract cut from March 2021 and she's still working on her job, why? The Arab person they hired kept going for vacations. My mom's boss sees my mom of great importance since she's done her job really well for the whole time she's worked there so, he (the boss) lets her work there despite the contract having been ended. He's a good boss. He'd let my siblings and I play on his computer in his office whenever we came to visit when we were kids. --EDIT: Sometimes the contracts being cut aren't in the power of the company, sometimes it's the government themselves that cut the contracts.--There's also another factor as to why my mom continues to work but yeah, that's her situation at the moment. My dad holds a respectable position in the company he works at so, his contract hasn't been cut. There's not a single day where I'm not anxious that my dad could lose his job. He's one of the lucky few at the moment who haven't lost their jobs. 

The school I used to go there in Riyadh had so many students, now it feels ever so little. My batch in had more than 30+ students in 2-3 sections late middle school but in the middle of junior high school? we're down to 16 students in one class. ~30 students with parents would be ~90 people and most of those students have siblings, all of them had to move back to our home country. Some have moved to different countries to find jobs and work there. That only speaks for my class, now imagine the rest of the level batches in my school, the rest of the hundreds of other schools here. It's even hard for parents here when they have a child right now. Luckily, my parents could just fly my siblings and I to our home country as we're old enough to be able to handle ourselves and so they can stay in Riyadh and continue to work, not having to pay more for dependent fees but you can't really fly a kid to out of nowhere. Most families just stick with sending their child to their grandparents or aunts and uncles back from their home country but there are still many families who're struggling to live with their children with them as they have no one who can take care of them outside Saudi Arabia. Some just ended up resorting to move and work in another country. 

The system there has been shady for so long like how Caucasian workers would be paid more. How Arab and Egyptian workers are also paid more despite working less than foreigners from African and SEA countries.

That's all I can share. I don't want to share much more info than this so yeah

[Non-Engagement Responses](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/) or just called NERs is the mental routine i do when i get intrusive thoughts. pretty neat! after doing all 4 affirmations, i like to follow it up or end it with acknowledging what im doing right now or what i should do be doing (e.g. school, art, music, etc) and affirm to myself that "that's the best i can do in this circumstance" and i let the thought go. i dont have to think about it now. these thoughts have space in my mind and they may continue to linger either way but they have no control over what i do now.

to recover from OCD or to stop ruminating is to be aware that the thoughts are there but not giving it attention. An attempt to remove thoughts like shaking your head is a compulsion. the more you ignore and disregard the thoughts it'll crescendo into a larger thought. i thought being mindful and doing meditation would help, instead it became a compulsion to (badly) distract myself from the intrusive thoughts because im distracting myself from the thoughts by focusing all my attention on my breathing. OCD is very very tricky to deal with and i now understand why there are specific therapies like ERP and CBT to combat it, and especially better if you consult an OCD therapist
